title: The refusal names the ruling, not just the config key
body:
One string, in `src/find_best_mobo/extract.py`. No behaviour change.

`extract_bundle` refuses before calling anything when `extraction_model` is empty. Its message told the reader to set the key but not that the answer was **already decided** — so a missing key read like an open question rather than a missing key.

It now names `docs/DESIGN.md` §6, which fixes the model by owner ruling (Opus 5, low effort for extraction). Everything else in the message stays: there is no default in code on purpose, because a chars-per-token factor measured against one model does not transfer to another, so a calibration record that cannot name its model is not evidence.

**This is the `src/` half of #205**, split out because a plan under `docs/plans/` may not change in the same pull request as the code it governs. The review gate blocked the combined version for exactly that, correctly — the rule is about what rides along, not how small or behaviour-neutral it is. The documents landed in #205; this is the remainder.

**No test, and why that is not a gap.** The diff changes the text of an existing error message on a path that already has coverage — `tests/test_extract.py` exercises the refusal. There is no new code path. `test-the-tests` correctly skips a diff with no new behaviour to revert.

1853 passing, `ruff check .` clean.
